transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess… I’m here because I don’t feel right at work anymore. It doesn’t feel safe to me, and I keep feeling like something’s wrong with me now. Like the person who was actually good at her job… isn’t really there anymore.
When did you start feeling this way about your job?
It started after the break-in… during that overnight deployment. So, about two years and four months ago.
Have you been feeling sad or depressed since the break-in?
I don’t know… I wouldn’t say sad exactly. Maybe worn down, but I haven’t really thought of it as depressed.
Do you often feel anxious or on edge?

Yeah… I guess so. I’m kind of always scanning things. Like on the train or in meetings, even just at lunch, I’m checking exits, noticing who’s too close, listening for sounds in the hallway. It’s hard to just… be there.
Have you been avoiding certain places or situations since the break-in?

Yeah… I guess I have. I try not to go through the lobby after dark. I’ll trade shifts or push back release windows if I can, and sometimes I just work from home or use the side entrance. It feels like… too much, like I’m going to fall apart if I have to walk through there.
Do you ever find yourself reliving the break-in?

Sometimes, yeah. Not like I’m choosing to think about it. A scanner beeps, or I hear heavy footsteps in the hall, or one of those late deployment alerts goes off… and suddenly I’m back in that office. My chest gets tight, and I can see the guard on the floor again. It kind of cuts through whatever I’m doing.
Do you try to avoid thinking about the break-in or memories related to it?

Yeah… I try not to go there in my head. Mostly I just arrange things so I don’t have to deal with reminders — trading shifts, pushing release windows, taking the side entrance, working from home if I can. Walking through that lobby after dark… it feels like I’m going to come apart.
Do you ever feel like you're outside of your body, watching yourself?
I don’t think so. Not really like watching myself from the outside… I haven’t noticed that.
Do you ever feel numb or disconnected from the world around you?
I’m not sure. I mean… I get quiet, but I wouldn’t say the world feels unreal or anything. I haven’t really noticed that.
Has your feeling of being 'worn down' or 'on edge' affected your relationships with friends or family?

A little, yeah. I’ve been more… short with people, I guess. It’s shown up more at work than with family — I’ve missed some migration deadlines, avoided late deployments, and I got called out in a review for conflicts that didn’t used to happen. I’ve also stopped doing mentoring and women-in-tech events. I just don’t feel steady enough for that right now.
Do you avoid talking or thinking about the break-in because it's too upsetting?

Yeah… I try not to get into it. I’ve been trading shifts and pushing back release windows so I don’t have to go through the lobby after dark. Sometimes I take the side entrance or just work from home if I can. It’s… too much. Like I’m going to fall apart if I have to deal with it.
Have you noticed any problems in your personal relationships or daily life because of these feelings or experiences?

Yeah… mostly at work. I’ve missed some migration deadlines and avoided late deployments, which isn’t like me. I got called out in a review for conflicts too… stuff that didn’t used to happen.

Outside of that, I’ve pulled back from mentoring and women-in-tech events. I just don’t feel steady enough to be reliable there right now.
Do you ever feel like you're in a daze or detached from yourself or your surroundings?
I don’t think so. Not really. Sometimes I kind of zone out, but… I wouldn’t say I feel detached from myself or anything like that.
Do you often think that you're permanently changed for the worse because of what happened during the break-in?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t like saying it, but it feels like work isn’t really safe anymore. And I keep feeling like… I’m not the same person I was before. Like the capable version of me kind of disappeared.
Do you often think that you're worthless or inadequate because of what happened during the break-in?
Yeah… sometimes. I don’t know if “worthless” is the word, but inadequate, maybe. Like I’m damaged now, and the person who was good at the job… the one who got promoted… isn’t really there anymore.
Do you feel guilty or ashamed about what happened during the break-in?

Yeah… ashamed, I guess. Guilty too. I keep going over it, like if I’d pushed harder for better security that night, or called sooner… maybe the guard wouldn’t have been hurt so badly. I know I was hiding and scared, but… it still feels like I should’ve done something.
Do you often think that you're unable to achieve your goals or be successful because of what happened during the break-in?

Yeah… I think so. It’s like since it happened, I can’t really picture being successful the same way. Work doesn’t feel safe anymore, and I feel… damaged, I guess. Like the competent person who got promoted isn’t really me now.
Do you believe you're a bad person because of what happened during the break-in?

I don’t know if I’d say “bad person.” But… yeah, I blame myself. I keep thinking if I’d insisted on better security for that overnight deployment, or called sooner, maybe the guard wouldn’t have gotten hurt so badly. Part of me knows I was hiding and terrified, but… it still feels like it’s on me.
